title: Reasoning Execution Substrate
abstract: This document records the approved ruling on what executes a reasoning kernel: deterministic code, or a language model constrained by an output schema. The ruling adopts Option A — deterministic kernels are the architecture, and the model-backed path under applications/investment/prototype risk rik/ is legacy, retained for reference and not canonical architecture § Recommendation, § Consequences . The source records that the decision was written down retrospectively, after the repository already contained two contradictory answers to the question status note . This is a Published ruling: approved by Piyush on 2026-08-04 § Approval Status .

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.html:
This document records the approved ruling on what executes a reasoning kernel: deterministic code, or a language model constrained by an output schema. The ruling adopts Option A — deterministic kernels are the architecture, and the model-backed path under applications/investment/prototype_risk_rik/ is legacy, retained for reference and not canonical architecture (§ Recommendation, § Consequences). The source records that the decision was written down retrospectively, after the repository already contained two contradictory answers to the question (status note).

This is a Published ruling: approved by Piyush on 2026-08-04 (§ Approval Status).

sections.heading: Research Question
sections.html:
The source states the question explicitly (§ Decision):

What executes a reasoning kernel: deterministic code, or a language model constrained by an output schema?

The source records that the question was live because the repository answered it both ways at once, in two places that do not reference each other, and that both are described as prototypes with neither described as superseding the other — "so a reader cannot tell which represents the intended architecture" (§ Decision).

sections.heading: Finding
sections.html:
The contradiction on record

The source tabulates the two contradictory answers found in the repository (§ Decision):

PathSubstrateSelf-description
choir_prototype/Deterministic Python, standard library only"No LLM call anywhere"
applications/investment/prototype_risk_rik/OpenAI Responses API, Pydantic-validated output"It does not represent live model reasoning" (of its deterministic provider only)

The options considered

The source sets out three options (§ Options), stated here in its own terms:

  • Option A — deterministic kernels are the architecture. Model-backed execution is exploratory work, retained as legacy and wound down. Kernels are code that reads an intermediate representation and emits a structured artifact.
  • Option B — model-backed kernels are the architecture. Kernels are model calls whose outputs are schema-validated. Determinism is abandoned or relocated to a caching or seeding layer.
  • Option C — both, at different tiers. Deterministic kernels for adjudication, model-backed extraction upstream of the IR.

Why Option B is rejected

The source identifies three CHOIR commitments as load-bearing here, and states that Option B "breaks all three at once" (§ Tradeoffs):

  1. Confidence is derived, never authored (confidence_framework.md §1). A model emitting a confidence field into a schema authors it. Schema validation checks the shape of the value, not its provenance. The source records that contracts.py currently defines QualitativeConfidence as an enum the provider fills in — "which is authorship with a type check on it."
  2. Independent agreement is evidence, not echo. Two kernels backed by the same model are not independent in the sense that makes agreement meaningful. The source names shared training data as a common cause, and states that "the prototype's whole argument for why agreement counts collapses."
  3. Replay and projection integrity (explainability_framework.md §1). A non-deterministic step means a record cannot be re-derived, so the execution-determinism and projection-integrity checks cannot hold.

Why Option C is not adopted now

The source describes Option C as "coherent in principle" and close to commitment #10 — neural retrieval, symbolic adjudication: embeddings propose, they never conclude (knowledge_graph_spec.md §2.5). It rules Option C out as a description of present practice on a factual ground, not a principled one: "It is not what the investment prototype does today: its model call produces the conclusion, not a retrieval candidate" (§ Tradeoffs).

Cost, and the ruling

The source records that Option A costs the least, on two stated grounds: the model-backed path is one isolated vertical slice under applications/, and the deterministic path "already carries the project's only measured result" (§ Tradeoffs).

The recommendation adopted is Option A — "the only option consistent with the project's stated thesis and with the three commitments above." The source qualifies this: Option C "remains available later for extraction upstream of the IR, where a proposing model concludes nothing — but that is a different decision, and adopting it should not be confused with keeping the current provider" (§ Recommendation).

What the ruling does and does not do

The consequences recorded (§ Consequences):

  • applications/investment/prototype_risk_rik/ is legacy. Its OpenAI provider is retained for reference and is not canonical architecture.
  • No new work should extend the model-backed path.
  • Retirement is not performed by this note. The source states that removing the legacy path "touches a passing test suite and a running UI, so it is scheduled work, not a side effect of writing a decision down."
  • requirements-dev.txt and pyproject.toml keep httpx while the legacy path exists. Both can be reviewed at retirement.

The source also records the provenance of the ruling itself: it was "recorded retrospectively — the repository already contained two contradictory answers to this question before the decision was written down" (status note).

sections.heading: Architectural Implications
sections.html:
The implications below are drawn from the source's own statements. The source has no section of this kind and does not itself present them as implications.

A reasoning kernel is deterministic code that reads an intermediate representation and emits a structured artifact (§ Options, Option A). The operative rule the source states is narrower than a general prohibition: "No new work should extend the model-backed path" (§ Consequences).

Three commitments constrain any future substrate proposal, because the source treats them as the test Option B failed: confidence must be derived rather than authored (confidence_framework.md §1); agreement between kernels counts as evidence only where the kernels are independent, which two kernels backed by the same model are not; and records must be re-derivable, or the execution-determinism and projection-integrity checks cannot hold (explainability_framework.md §1) (§ Tradeoffs).

Model-backed components are not excluded from the architecture in general, but their admissible position is bounded: upstream of the IR, as extraction where "a proposing model concludes nothing," consistent with neural retrieval, symbolic adjudication: embeddings propose, they never conclude (knowledge_graph_spec.md §2.5). Admitting such a component is a separate decision that this ruling does not make (§ Recommendation).

The legacy path continues to exist; the source records that removing it "touches a passing test suite and a running UI," so the ruling constrains new work rather than immediately removing the old (§ Consequences).

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.html:
The source records the following unresolved or deferred items:

  • Option C is deferred, not decided. Adopting model-backed extraction upstream of the IR "remains available later" but is "a different decision" that this note does not make (§ Recommendation).
  • Retirement of the legacy path is scheduled work, not done. The source states that retirement "is not performed by this note" and is "scheduled work" because it touches a passing test suite and a running UI (§ Consequences). The source does not record when that work is to be carried out.
  • Dependency cleanup is deferred. requirements-dev.txt and pyproject.toml keep httpx while the legacy path exists; "both can be reviewed at retirement" (§ Consequences).
  • QualitativeConfidence in contracts.py is recorded as non-conforming — an enum the provider fills in, described as "authorship with a type check on it" (§ Tradeoffs). The source records the defect; it does not record a remediation.
  • The decision is retrospective. The source notes the repository held two contradictory answers before the decision was written down (status note); it does not record what else was built against the unresolved contradiction.
